criteria.description: Correctly explains the geometric rank-deficiency at full stretch (no joint combination moves the end-effector radially outward).
Correctly connects rank(J)<d to JJ^T becoming singular.
Correctly explains why adding W>0 keeps J^T C J + W invertible.

solutions.fullSolution:
At full stretch, every joint's instantaneous motion moves the end-effector only tangentially (perpendicular to the fully extended arm); no combination of joint velocities can move it directly outward/inward along the arm's own direction. This means the columns of J no longer span all d output directions: rank(J)<d, a genuine rank deficiency.
When rank(J)<d, JJ^T is singular (non-invertible), so the naive pseudo-inverse J^T(JJ^T)^-1 requires inverting a singular matrix, causing numerical blowup (an IK step could demand unbounded joint velocity).
Adding W>0 inside (J^T C J + W)^-1 shifts J^T C J's eigenvalues up (MATH-04's shift-invariance fact), guaranteeing the sum stays strictly positive definite and invertible even when J^T C J alone is singular, the same ridge-regression/Levenberg-Marquardt fix used elsewhere in this course, here preventing IK from ever requesting an unbounded joint velocity near a singularity.
